subject: Private endpoint egress: IPs, firewall policy, and rotation commitments
messages:

Subject: Private endpoint egress: IP ranges & firewall expectations

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As we lock down our perimeter for the Acme private deployment we need: 1) the list of egress IPs (or a signed manifest) that Redwood's runtime will use to reach external services (control plane, metrics endpoints, updates), 2) a clear statement on whether you support static NAT for private deployments, and 3) your policy on rotation and notification windows if IPs change.

Our security team (copied) will use this to create the allowlist and firewall rules. A couple specifics they asked for:
- Are FQDN-based allowlists supported (SNI) as a fallback?
- If you publish an IP manifest, is there an audit artifact we can store (signed PDF or CSV)?
- For ephemeral pools, what advance notice can customers expect (days)?

Can you provide a short artifact we can attach to our procurement packet (SOC2 evidence will be required later).

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement timelines are tight.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Security Lead, Acme Medical
pshah@acmemed.com

---

(attachment request) Please include any sample firewall rule snippets and a manifest if possible.
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress: IP ranges & firewall expectations

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our current exported manifest and a short evidence PDF that summarizes our egress posture for private deployments. See attachments: redwood-egress-ip-blocks.csv, egress-evidence.pdf.

Short answers here:
- Static NAT: yes, for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments we can allocate a reserved NAT pool that is stable for the contract term (option we outline below).
- FQDN/SNI: we support FQDN allowlisting (SNI) as a fallback for services that rely on hostname-based routing, but we recommend IP allowlisting for service endpoints that do not guarantee SNI (some managed services do TLS SNI, others terminate earlier).
- Rotation notice: we offer two modes — (A) Reserved pool: no rotation during the reserved term; (B) Ephemeral pool: rotation with a 14-day minimum notification window (webhook and artifact).

For convenience here is the quick control-plane vs data-plane nuance:
- Control plane (account management, billing, control APIs): egress is via our control-plane network (manifest attached).
- Data plane (model inference traffic): in Private deployments this stays inside the customer's VPC where applicable; outbound for runtime updates, telemetry, or package pulls uses the egress manifest above.

I'll put a recommended firewall snippet in a follow-up message and capture the options we can present in the SOW.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-egress-ip-blocks.csv (CSV, list of /24 blocks and CIDRs), egress-evidence.pdf (signed PDF summary)

Dylan — thanks, that helps. A couple follow-ups from our network team:

> On Mon, 13 Jul 2026 at 10:02, Dylan Brooks wrote:
> > For convenience here is the quick control-plane vs data-plane nuance: ...

1) The CSV looks like a list of /24s — do you have an option to publish a single static /28 per customer (smaller attack surface) if we sign a longer term commitment?
2) If you rotate the ephemeral pool can you provide: a signed manifest + a daily delta (what changed) + a machine-readable webhook to pull the new list? Our change window requires automated ingestion.
3) Regarding SNI: we can't rely solely on SNI for several managed vendor services that are behind CDNs. We need an explicit minimum commitment on IP stability for endpoints used in production.

Also: procurement has asked for a redlineable amendment that guarantees at least 30 days' notice for any IP changes that would block production traffic. Can you flag if that's acceptable?

Thanks,
Priya

Acme Networking (gcp-net@acmemed.com) added a note: please include firewall port/egress snippets for common telemetry endpoints (metrics, healthchecks, package fetch), and list the TLS ports we use.

Priya / Acme team — summarizing the technical proposal and including sample firewall rule snippets below. We tried to keep options explicit so your security and procurement teams can pick what maps to their risk profile.

Proposal (final):
- Option A (Reserved static): Redwood binds a dedicated NAT pool to Acme (single /28 per prod env or configurable). We treat this as a contractual, non-rotating pool for the committed term (recommended 12 months). Change notifications: 30 days.
- Option B (Webhook manifest): Redwood publishes a signed CSV manifest daily and a delta feed. Ephemeral IP ranges rotate but we guarantee 14 days' notice before any IP in the active set is removed; machine-readable webhook available on request.

Sample firewall allow rules (suggested minimal set):
# Allow control plane (TLS)
- Src: Acme-Private-Subnet (your infra)
- Dst: 198.51.100.0/24 (example from attached CSV)
- Ports: 443, 5222
- Protocol: TCP
- Description: Redwood control-plane API + cert pin validation

# Allow telemetry / metrics endpoint
- Dst: 203.0.113.10/32
- Ports: 443
- Protocol: TCP
- Description: Telemetry ingest (TLS only)

Notes on TLS & SNI: all public endpoints require TLS 1.2+ and certificate validation. We recommend combining IP allowlist + FQDN checks for defense-in-depth. If you cannot rely on SNI for a specific vendor endpoint, use the static reserved option to avoid surprises.

Operational commitments:
- Signed manifest (daily) and weekly audited PDF (stored to shared Drive)
- Webhook for delta and full manifests (HMAC-signed)
- DocuSign amendment for 30-day notice if Option A selected

Next steps:
1) Marissa: please send the DocuSign amendment (HS-8943).
2) Acme security: confirm whether you prefer Option A (reserved /28) or Option B (webhook manifest).
3) After selection: we will produce a final redlined SOW with the policy language and example firewall snippets in the contract attachment.

--
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com
